title: The Staircase at Aubazine: the Orphan, the Rue Cambon, and the Room at the Ritz
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Charity Ward and the Cafe-Concert

stops.name: Saumur, birth in the charity hospital
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the coordinate is a town-centre approximation, because the ward and building footprint within Saumur are not independently pinpointed in any source consulted
stops.campa: In the charity hospital of Saumur, run by the Sisters of Providence, a laundrywoman named Eugenie Jeanne Devolle gives birth to a daughter. The father, Albert Chanel, is an itinerant market trader; the parents will marry the following year. The child is registered Gabrielle Bonheur Chanel. She will spend the next eighty-seven years giving other accounts of her beginnings: the aunts, the horses, the mother remembered as a beauty. All of them are built over this ward, and the ward itself she never once names in public.
suggested_refs: The birth register of Saumur, 19 August 1883, and the hospice civil of the Sisters of Providence
sources: Justine Picardie, Coco Chanel: The Legend and the Life (2010)

stops.name: Brive-la-Gaillarde, the mother dies
stops.date_confidence: contradiction unresolved: the death is dated 6 February 1895 at Brive-la-Gaillarde in the French record and given as 1894 in one summary the research pass rejected; the mother's age at death is 31 in the French record and 32 in the English, and the discrepancy is left standing. The exact address within Brive is undocumented
stops.campa: Jeanne Devolle dies at Brive-la-Gaillarde of tuberculosis and a life spent following a market trader from town to town. Gabrielle is eleven. Albert Chanel disperses the five children rather than keep them: the sons out to farm labour, the daughters to the nuns. He does not come back for them. The French record gives the mother's age at death as thirty-one and the English record gives thirty-two, and the daughter who will spend a lifetime revising this month never settles the number either.
suggested_refs: The death act of Jeanne Devolle, Brive-la-Gaillarde, February 1895

stops.name: Aubazine, the abbey orphanage
stops.date_confidence: the placement is anchored to the mother's death in February 1895 and dated here to the month after it; no admission record is quoted in any source consulted. The departure is given as 1900 or 1901 depending on the account
stops.campa: The Cistercian abbey of Saint-Etienne in the Correze takes the two Chanel girls into its orphanage, run by the Congregation du Sacre-Coeur de Marie. The nuns teach sewing. The building teaches the rest: black habits against white walls, the interlocking arcs of the rose windows, a stone staircase turning on itself. The house of Chanel will later name all of it as the source of the palette and the doubled C, and Chanel herself will spend her life refusing to say she was ever in this place.
suggested_refs: The Abbaye Saint-Etienne at Aubazine, its rose windows and its stone stair

stops.name: Moulins, the boarding house and the name
stops.date_confidence: attested year for the move to Moulins; the month is not recorded and defaults to January. The cabaret work is dated 1903 in the record and the venue is not consistently named, so the coordinate marks the town
stops.campa: At eighteen she is moved to a Catholic boarding house in Moulins for girls of small means, and from there into a shop as a seamstress. At night she sings at the garrison cafe-concerts, with two numbers in her repertoire: 'Ko Ko Ri Ko' and 'Qui qu'a vu Coco.' The soldiers call for the second and then call her by it. She keeps the name for seventy years and puts it on the door of every shop she owns, and she is never again addressed by the one the registrar wrote down at Saumur.
suggested_refs: The garrison cafe-concerts of Moulins and the song 'Qui qu'a vu Coco'
sources: Edmonde Charles-Roux, Chanel: Her Life, Her World (1975)

stops.name: Vichy, the pump room at the Grande Grille
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded. The identification of the specific thermal establishment as the Grande Grille is tagged reconstruction in the research pass and is not firm
stops.campa: She goes to Vichy to become a stage singer, and the spa town, full of professionals, judges the voice too small. She takes work instead handing mineral water to the cure-takers at the pump room, watching a season of rich people drink their glasses at the prescribed hour and change clothes four times a day. She is twenty-three, with no trade and no protector. The stage career ends here. It is the last job she holds in which someone else sets the wages.
suggested_refs: The thermal pump rooms of Vichy in the 1906 season

stops.name: Chateau de Royallieu, three years as Balsan's mistress
stops.date_confidence: attested year for the beginning of the liaison; no month recorded. The residence runs roughly 1906 to 1909, and the coordinate approximates the Royallieu quarter of Compiegne rather than a confirmed chateau footprint
stops.campa: Etienne Balsan, cavalry officer and textile heir, installs her at his chateau near Compiegne, where the sporting rich of the Belle Epoque keep horses and mistresses in roughly equal number. She rides and she hunts. She is bored. To fill the mornings she makes hats for herself, plain straw boaters stripped of the birds and the flowers everyone else is wearing, and the other women in the house begin asking where they can get one. Three years pass at Royallieu. She leaves it a milliner.
suggested_refs: The Chateau de Royallieu at Compiegne, Balsan's racing establishment

stops.name: Paris, 160 boulevard Malesherbes: Boy Capel
stops.date_confidence: attested year for the beginning of the affair with Capel; no month recorded. The apartment is documented in the biographies rather than in a lease
stops.campa: Balsan lends her his Paris apartment on the boulevard Malesherbes and she works out of it, trimming hats at a table, selling to the women she met at Royallieu. Arthur Capel, an English businessman and Balsan's friend, called Boy by everyone, becomes her lover in this apartment and then her banker. The arrangement is the ordinary one of the period; its terms are not. He lends against a business rather than against her, and she treats what he lends as a debt with a date on it.
suggested_refs: Balsan's apartment at 160 boulevard Malesherbes, first workroom of the house

stops.name: Paris, 21 rue Cambon: Chanel Modes
stops.date_confidence: attested year for the millinery licence and the opening; no month recorded. The Dorziat performance in Bel Ami is separately attested to 1912
stops.campa: She takes a licence as a milliner and opens Chanel Modes on the ground floor at 21 rue Cambon, Capel's money behind the lease. The building's owner forbids her to make dresses, because a couturier upstairs holds that right. Two years later the actress Gabrielle Dorziat wears her hats onstage in Bel Ami and the name travels past the women who already knew it. Chanel will spend the next sixty years moving along this one street, buying number by number, and will work from no other.
suggested_refs: The shopfront at 21 rue Cambon, first premises under her own name

stops.name: Deauville, the jersey shop on the rue Gontaut-Biron
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded
stops.campa: Capel finances a second shop in the Normandy resort, on the rue Gontaut-Biron. She sells jersey, a knit used until then for men's underwear, cut loose and worn without a corset, to women who have come for the sea air and cannot breathe in what they brought with them. War is declared the following year and Deauville fills with people who have left Paris. The clothes that let a woman move turn out to be the clothes for it, and she is the only one in the town selling them.
suggested_refs: The Deauville boutique of 1913 and the first jersey sportswear

segments.name: The House on the Rue Cambon

stops.name: Biarritz, the couture house opposite the casino
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded
stops.campa: She opens a full couture house in a villa facing the casino at Biarritz, near enough to neutral Spain to draw the Russian and Spanish aristocracy sitting out the war with money that still moves. Within a year the house is in profit. She repays Boy Capel every franc he has put into her, and the loan closes. It is the only debt of her life she settles early, and from this point the money in the business is hers, made by selling clothes to women who are frightened and want to look calm.
suggested_refs: The Biarritz maison of 1915, first full couture house of the name

stops.name: Paris, 31 rue Cambon: the building and the maison
stops.date_confidence: attested year for the purchase and 1919 for the registration as couturiere; no months recorded
stops.campa: She buys the building at 31 rue Cambon and registers the following year as a couturiere, which makes the maison de couture legal and the millinery licence beside the point. By 1927 she owns numbers 23 through 31. Inside she has built the mirrored staircase she will sit on during every collection for the rest of her life, watching the salon below in fragments, seen by nobody in it. The address becomes the fixed point of a life that otherwise never stops moving between hotels.
suggested_refs: The mirrored staircase at 31 rue Cambon and the private apartment above the salon

stops.name: Near Frejus, the crash on the Riviera road
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; sources disagree on the stretch of road, some placing the crash nearer Cannes than Frejus, and the night drive to the wreck is traditional rather than documented
stops.campa: Boy Capel, driving south on the Riviera road, is killed when the car leaves it. He had married an English aristocrat the year before and had gone on keeping Chanel, who by then no longer needed keeping. She is driven through the night to the wreck and sits by the road until morning. Nine years of her life and every franc of her first capital came from this man. She is thirty-six and rich, and by her own account, given to Paul Morand a quarter of a century later, finished with happiness.
stops.quote: His death was a terrible blow to me. In losing Capel, I lost everything. What followed was not a life of happiness, I have to say.
stops.quote_source: Chanel to Paul Morand, recalled roughly twenty-five years after the event; Morand's conversations were published as L'Allure de Chanel, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The stretch of the Route Nationale 7 where Capel's car left the road, 22 December 1919

stops.name: Garches, Villa Bel Respiro: the Stravinskys
stops.date_confidence: the introduction through Diaghilev is dated spring 1920 and the lodging at Bel Respiro September 1920 to May 1921; the stop is dated to the beginning of the tenancy. The alleged affair is disputed by the Stravinsky family and is not settled here
stops.campa: Diaghilev brings Igor Stravinsky to her in the spring; by September the composer, his wife Catherine, and their four children are living in her villa at Garches, exiles from a revolution with nowhere else to go. Chanel pays for the household. She has also, that year, underwritten the Ballets Russes revival of Le Sacre du Printemps with three hundred thousand francs on the condition that nobody be told who did it. An affair between her and Stravinsky is alleged by biographers and denied by his family.
suggested_refs: Villa Bel Respiro at Garches, and the 1920 revival of Le Sacre du Printemps

stops.name: La Bocca, near Cannes: the fifth vial
stops.date_confidence: the numbered samples were presented in 1920 and the perfume went on sale 5 May 1921; the stop is dated to the presentation and the month is not recorded. Sources disagree on whether the formulating laboratory stood at La Bocca or in Grasse itself, and the coordinate has been moved west from a value that landed in Cannes proper
stops.campa: Ernest Beaux, a perfumer trained in Russia and working the fields around Grasse for jasmine and rose, brings her numbered vials, samples one through five and twenty through twenty-four. She chooses the fifth and keeps the number as the name. The scent goes on sale on the fifth of May, 1921, carrying aldehydes at a dose nobody had used before, so that it smells of no flower in particular. The claim that it is the first perfume to bear a couturier's name is false: Paul Poiret's Rosine came a decade earlier.
suggested_refs: Ernest Beaux's numbered submissions of 1920 and the launch of Chanel No. 5 on 5 May 1921

segments.name: The Ballets Russes and the Wertheimers

stops.name: Paris, Longchamp: the meeting with Pierre Wertheimer
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded. The coordinate is the Longchamp racecourse itself, supplied to place a meeting the research pass located by name but not by coordinate
stops.campa: Theophile Bader of the Galeries Lafayette, who wants No. 5 in his store and cannot get enough of it, introduces her at the Longchamp racecourse to Pierre Wertheimer, whose family owns Bourjois and knows how to make scent by the ton. Chanel has a perfume selling faster than she can produce it and no factory. Wertheimer has factories. The meeting lasts an afternoon. The company that comes out of it, Parfums Chanel, outlives both of them and holds the perfume still.
suggested_refs: The Longchamp racecourse, and Theophile Bader's role as broker between Chanel and Bourjois

stops.name: Paris, 31 rue Cambon: the Parfums Chanel agreement
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month or day recorded in the sources consulted
stops.campa: The contract creating Parfums Chanel gives the Wertheimers seventy per cent, Bader twenty for making the introduction, and Chanel ten, as a stockholder withdrawn from operations. She signs it because she is a couturiere and regards perfume as a sideline. For the next twenty years she litigates against it. In private she gives Pierre Wertheimer a single standing epithet, and in 1941 she will try to have his company taken off him by an occupying power on the ground that his family is Jewish.
stops.quote_source: Chanel on Pierre Wertheimer, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The 1924 Parfums Chanel agreement and its 70/20/10 division

stops.name: Paris, Theatre des Champs-Elysees: Le Train Bleu
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Her costumes for Le Train Bleu open at the Theatre des Champs-Elysees, a Ballets Russes piece about vacationers on the Riviera, danced in bathing costumes and knitted sweaters she designs out of her own sportswear. It is her first major commission for a stage and it ties her name publicly to Diaghilev's company, which she is also financing without saying so. The dancers wear what her clients wear, and the audience recognizes the clothes before it recognizes the ballet.
suggested_refs: Le Train Bleu, Theatre des Champs-Elysees, 20 June 1924, costumes by Chanel

stops.name: New York, American Vogue: the little black dress
stops.date_confidence: attested year of publication; no month recorded, and no editorial address for Vogue appears in any source consulted, so the coordinate stands in for the New York garment trade rather than an office
stops.campa: American Vogue prints a Chanel dress in black, long-sleeved and unornamented, and compares it to the Ford: one model, one colour, available to everyone. The comparison is offered as praise, because in 1926 standardization is a modern virtue. Black until then belongs to mourning and to servants. The dress takes it off both of them and hands it to women who can afford anything they like, which is exactly what makes the plainness expensive and the copy, a season later, cheap.
suggested_refs: The 1926 American Vogue plate of the Chanel 'Ford' dress

stops.name: Monte Carlo, the Duke of Westminster
stops.date_confidence: the meeting is dated 1923 in one lens and 1923 to 1924 in another; no month is recorded, and the site is disputed, some accounts placing the introduction aboard a yacht rather than at the casino
stops.campa: She is introduced at Monte Carlo to Hugh Grosvenor, second Duke of Westminster, called Bendor, reckoned the richest man in England. The affair runs about ten years. He gives her emeralds, land on the Riviera, and the run of a circuit of estates in three countries; she goes on running her business through all of it and does not marry him. Accounts differ on where the two of them met, casino or yacht, and the atlas keeps the casino without insisting that it is the right room.
suggested_refs: The Casino de Monte-Carlo and the Grosvenor circle of the mid-1920s

stops.name: Mimizan, Chateau Woolsack
stops.date_confidence: attested to the interwar decade rather than to a year; 1925 is a placement inside the run of the affair, not a dated visit. The coordinate has been moved north from a value some eleven kilometres south of the town
stops.campa: The Duke keeps a villa in the pines behind the Landes coast, Chateau Woolsack, built for him in 1911 by Detmar Blow and Fernand Billerey. Chanel is among the interwar guests who come down to it, one address in a rotation that also takes in Cheshire, Sutherland, and a yacht. She is running a couture house of several hundred employees from the middle of this, by telegram and by train, and going back to the rue Cambon between visits to fit the collections herself.
suggested_refs: Chateau Woolsack at Mimizan, built 1911 for the Duke of Westminster

stops.name: Eaton Hall, Cheshire: the house parties
stops.date_confidence: attested to the 1920s; no year or month is fixed for any single visit, and 1926 is a placement inside the decade. The coordinate has been moved north from a value some three kilometres south of the house
stops.campa: Eaton Hall in Cheshire is the Grosvenor family's principal seat, and Chanel is a frequent guest in it through the twenties, moving among house parties and shooting weeks in a world with no interest whatever in the ateliers that pay for her. She dresses for it in the Duke's own idiom, borrowed and re-cut. Their taste she thinks heavy. What she takes out of these rooms is their cloth, and the discovery that a woman can wear men's fabric and not look like a man.
suggested_refs: Eaton Hall, Cheshire, seat of the Dukes of Westminster

stops.name: Achfary, Sutherland: the tweed
stops.date_confidence: attested loosely to the late 1920s and dated here by placement; the exact estate and the dates of any stay are not rigorously sourced. The coordinate has been corrected by some thirteen kilometres to the Grosvenor holding at Achfary
stops.campa: At the Grosvenor shooting estate in Sutherland she fishes and shoots, and wears the men's tweeds and knitted jerseys of the household, because on a Scottish hill there is nothing else to wear. The cloth goes home with her. Within a few seasons the Scottish mills are weaving to her order and the tweed suit is a Chanel garment, taken off gamekeepers and gentlemen and sold to women in Paris and New York at prices no gamekeeper could say aloud. The Chanel suit is first cut in 1923 and this is where it gets its cloth.
suggested_refs: The Grosvenor estate at Achfary, Sutherland, and the Scottish mills that first wove for Chanel

stops.name: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, Villa La Pausa
stops.date_confidence: built 1928 to 1929; no month recorded. The coordinate has been corrected by some three kilometres west from a value that landed near Menton
stops.campa: On land the Duke gives her above Roquebrune-Cap-Martin she builds La Pausa with the architect Robert Streitz, and has him model the main staircase on the one at the abbey of Aubazine. She has spent thirty years refusing to speak of the orphanage. She puts its staircase in her own house, in stone, and walks down it every summer for twenty-five years. It is the only house she ever builds rather than rents, and the last of her addresses that is not a hotel.
suggested_refs: Villa La Pausa and Robert Streitz's stair after Aubazine

stops.name: Venice, Isola di San Michele: Diaghilev's funeral
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the death; the burial follows within days and is dated here to the death. The identity of the payer is contested and unresolved
stops.campa: Sergei Diaghilev dies in Venice at fifty-seven, in debt, and is buried on the cemetery island. The record has Misia Sert at the bedside and paying for the funeral. That Chanel paid, secretly, on condition that her name be kept out of it, is a claim carried by biographers and by the house, and the two accounts stand side by side here without being reconciled. What is not disputed is that Chanel came, and that she stood at the grave beside Misia. The man who had brought her the Ballets Russes is in it.
suggested_refs: Diaghilev's grave in the Orthodox section of San Michele, Venice

stops.name: Culver City, MGM: the Hollywood contract
stops.date_confidence: the offer is dated 1931 at Monte Carlo and the California trip 1931, corrected from a summary that placed the journey in 1932; the second commission, for Ina Claire, falls in 1932. No months recorded
stops.campa: Samuel Goldwyn, met at Monte Carlo, offers a reported million dollars for two Hollywood trips a year to dress the stars. She travels out in 1931 with Misia Sert and dresses Gloria Swanson for Tonight or Never; the following year Ina Claire wears her clothes in The Greeks Had a Word for Them. She finds the place infantile and vulgar and says so where it can be printed. The studios find her clothes insufficiently exaggerated for the camera. The contract lapses and she does not go back.
stops.quote_source: Chanel on Hollywood, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The MGM lot at Culver City and the Goldwyn contract of 1931

stops.name: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, the death of Paul Iribe
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded in the sources consulted. The morphine characterization is drawn from biographical research and is not a finding of any court or medical record
stops.campa: Paul Iribe, illustrator, her companion of several years, dies suddenly at La Pausa. She had financed his newsletter Le Temoin, an ultra-nationalist and openly antisemitic sheet, for as long as it ran. By this year the biographical record describes her as injecting herself with morphine every day, a habit she keeps to the end. Her couture business employs about four thousand people. She is fifty-two, without a partner and without children, and she runs the largest fashion house in France.
suggested_refs: Le Temoin, the newsletter Chanel financed, and its editorial line
sources: Hal Vaughan, Sleeping with the Enemy: Coco Chanel's Secret War (2011)

stops.name: Paris, Hotel Ritz: the permanent suite
stops.date_confidence: attested from 1937; no month recorded. The pin is the atlas canonical Ritz coordinate, inherited unchanged from the christian_dior and eva_peron files
stops.campa: She moves into the Hotel Ritz on the place Vendome, a few hundred metres from her workrooms, and lives there. She keeps the suite for the rest of her life and calls no other place home. Marcel Proust had worked this same building fifteen years earlier, buying society gossip off the maitre d'hotel at hours when the dining room was empty. In 1947 Eva Peron will receive Christian Dior and Fath and Rochas in a suite upstairs. The Ritz keeps handing the atlas the same address, and Chanel is its middle term.
suggested_refs: The Ritz suite on the place Vendome, later renamed for her

stops.name: Paris, 31 rue Cambon: the house closes
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of the declaration of war; the day the ateliers actually shut is not recorded
stops.campa: At the declaration of war she shuts the couture house, all of it, and puts some four thousand women out of work in a week, saying that it is not a time for fashion. The boutique at number 31 stays open to sell perfume and accessories. Christian Dior spends the same war inside Lucien Lelong's house, kept open by order of the Chambre Syndicale and dressing the wives of German officers; Chanel closes the ateliers and sells scent to the same customers. Two answers to one occupation.
stops.quote_source: Chanel on closing the couture house, 1939, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The closure order of September 1939 and the boutique licence that survived it

stops.name: Paris, Hotel Ritz: Hans Gunther von Dincklage
stops.date_confidence: attested year for the beginning of the relationship; no month recorded. Vaughan dates Dincklage's intelligence career from 1928, while Dincklage's own record begins at the German embassy in Paris in the spring of 1933, and the earlier date rests on Vaughan alone
stops.campa: The Ritz is requisitioned in part as quarters for senior German officers, and Chanel stays on in it. She begins a relationship with Baron Hans Gunther von Dincklage, a German aristocrat attached to the embassy in Paris since 1933 and working in military and SD intelligence. He is thirteen years younger than she is. The liaison secures her rooms, her rations, and her freedom of movement for four years, in a city where all three are rationed by the same authority.
suggested_refs: The German requisition of the place Vendome side of the Ritz, 1940

stops.name: Paris, the Aryanization petition
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day as reported through L'Express (2005); the archival document itself was not inspected in this research pass
stops.campa: She petitions the occupation authorities to take Parfums Chanel from the Wertheimers under the Aryanization laws, arguing that the business is still the property of Jews, that its owners have abandoned it, and that she is owed reparation for the harm suffered over these seventeen years. The Wertheimers had seen it coming: in May 1940 they signed nominal control over to a Christian industrialist, Felix Amiot, who held it through the war and gave it back afterward. The petition fails. She never withdraws it.
stops.quote: sont toujours la propriete de Juifs
stops.quote_source: Chanel's petition regarding Parfums Chanel, 5 May 1941, quoted in the French Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel' citing L'Express (2005)
suggested_refs: The 5 May 1941 petition and the Amiot transfer of May 1940

stops.name: Berlin, Prinz-Albrecht-Strasse 8: Walter Schellenberg
stops.date_confidence: contradiction unresolved and tagged reconstruction: one lens of the research pass asserted the Berlin journey flatly, the other recorded that Chanel's own postwar statements and several biographers deny she travelled this leg, attributing it to Dincklage or to intermediaries. The hedge is adopted here. No month recorded
stops.campa: In Hal Vaughan's reconstruction from wartime intelligence files, Chanel travels toward Berlin and meets Walter Schellenberg, head of SD foreign intelligence, at the Reich Security Main Office on the Prinz-Albrecht-Strasse, and he backs the scheme built around her. Schellenberg's postwar interrogators record his reason for using her. Chanel denied ever making this journey, and several biographers give the leg to Dincklage instead. Her denial and Vaughan's files both stay in the record here.
stops.quote: a person who knew Churchill sufficiently to undertake political negotiations
stops.quote_source: Walter Schellenberg on Chanel, from postwar British interrogation records, quoted in secondary summary via the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The RSHA building on Prinz-Albrecht-Strasse and Schellenberg's postwar interrogation file

stops.name: Madrid, Hotel Ritz: Operation Modellhut
stops.date_confidence: dated November 1943 to early 1944 in Vaughan; the stop takes the opening month and no day is recorded
stops.campa: Operation Modellhut sends her to Madrid, where she stays at the Ritz and waits for a channel to Winston Churchill carrying a separate-peace overture from inside German intelligence. Captain Walter Kutschmann handles her money in the city. In Vichy the same season, Louis Vuitton's shop is the one ground-floor tenant Petain's government leaves trading in the Hotel du Parc, and Le Corbusier is in the same town pressing his urbanism on the same regime. The atlas keeps finding French luxury inside the apparatus.
suggested_refs: The Madrid Ritz in 1943 and the Modellhut file in British and French intelligence archives

stops.name: Madrid, British Embassy: the courier turns
stops.date_confidence: dated late 1943 to early 1944; the stop takes the later bound and no month or day is recorded. The episode rests on Vaughan's reading of declassified files, and some later biographers treat its detail as unresolved
stops.campa: Vera Bate Lombardi, an English-born friend recruited as courier and told the trip concerns opening a Madrid boutique, carries the letter meant for Churchill to the embassy on the Calle Fernando el Santo. There she denounces Chanel and Dincklage to the British as Nazi spies, and the mission ends in that room. In Metzingen the same year Hugo Boss runs a uniform factory for the Reich with a photograph of himself beside Hitler on the office wall. The clothing trade keeps arriving at this war by different roads.
stops.quote_source: Vera Bate Lombardi's denunciation to the British Embassy in Madrid, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The British Embassy at Calle Fernando el Santo and the Lombardi denunciation

stops.name: Paris, the purge committee
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; the day is not recorded and the exact building of the interrogation is not consistently named, so the coordinate approximates the central Paris administrative sites of the period
stops.campa: The Free French purge committee takes her in for questioning on collaboration weeks after the Liberation, and releases her within hours for want of documented evidence. Before she leaves for Switzerland she puts word out at the rue Cambon that American soldiers may have a bottle of No. 5 each, free, and the queue runs down the street. Some historians hold that Churchill had the ambassador Duff Cooper intervene to keep her out of court. No order has ever been found.
stops.quote_source: Chanel to her grand-niece Gabrielle Palasse Labrunie on returning home after the September 1944 interrogation, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The epuration files of September 1944 and the queue for No. 5 at the rue Cambon

stops.name: Lausanne, the nine years of exile
stops.date_confidence: attested from 1945 to the early 1950s; no month recorded. Chanel's support of Schellenberg can only run from his release in 1951 to his death in 1952, and the open-ended phrasing in one lens has been bounded here
stops.campa: She leaves for Switzerland and stays the better part of nine years, living for part of them with Dincklage, who had fled to Lausanne ahead of her. She pays him. She also pays Walter Schellenberg between his release in 1951 and his death the following year, and covers the cost of his funeral in Turin; biographers read the payments as the price of silence. Dincklage ends in Mallorca and dies there in 1974. Through all of it the rue Cambon salon is shut and only the perfume trades.
suggested_refs: The Swiss years, and the payments to Dincklage and Schellenberg

stops.name: Paris, the settlement with Pierre Wertheimer
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the lump sum is given in 2022 dollar terms in the source and no franc figure is quoted
stops.campa: She stops fighting Pierre Wertheimer in the courts and settles with him instead. On the seventeenth of May the terms are agreed: a lump sum worth roughly twelve million dollars in present money, two per cent of Chanel No. 5 sales worldwide, and Wertheimer's undertaking to pay her living expenses for the rest of her life. The man whose family business she had tried to have seized under German law now underwrites her. Neither of them puts 1941 in the document, and neither of them forgets it.
suggested_refs: The 17 May 1947 renegotiation of the 1924 Parfums Chanel contract

stops.name: Paris, the Vaufreland case
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded, and the canonical Paris coordinate stands in because no court address appears in the sources consulted
stops.campa: She is summoned back to Paris for the war-crimes case against Baron Louis de Vaufreland, the wartime associate through whom the intelligence services first wrote her name down, and she denies every accusation put to her. Asked to account for herself, she offers the investigating judge a character reference from the British ambassador. Nothing comes of the case against her. The Prefecture de Police file, with its pseudonym Westminster and its agent reference F 7124, stays in the archive another sixty-two years.
stops.quote: I could arrange for a declaration to come from Mr. Duff Cooper.
stops.quote_source: Chanel to the investigating judge, 1949 Cour de Justice proceedings against Louis de Vaufreland, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The Cour de Justice file on Louis de Vaufreland and Chanel's 1949 deposition

stops.name: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, La Pausa sold
stops.date_confidence: attested year; no month recorded
stops.campa: She sells La Pausa to the publisher Emery Reves, and with it the staircase copied from Aubazine, the terraces, and the last thing the Duke of Westminster gave her. She is seventy, out of the business fourteen years, and watching Christian Dior's New Look put women back into boned waists and petticoats, which she regards as men dressing women again. She never owns a house again, and what she does next she does with Pierre Wertheimer's money rather than her own.
suggested_refs: The 1953 sale of La Pausa to Emery and Wendy Reves

stops.name: Paris, 31 rue Cambon: the comeback collection
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the collection; the American Vogue appearance of Marie-Helene Arnaud is attested to March 1954 and the Seventh Avenue copying to 1954 and 1955
stops.campa: At seventy she reopens the couture house on the rue Cambon with a collection financed in full by Pierre Wertheimer. The French press is cold and says why: the war. The American and British press are not, and by March, when Marie-Helene Arnaud appears in American Vogue in a Chanel suit, the orders start. Seventh Avenue copies the suit at every price, and the American market rather than the French one restores her. Across town Cristobal Balenciaga is cutting in the opposite direction. Of him she says in this same decade both that he alone is a couturier in the truest sense and that he dislikes women.
suggested_refs: The comeback collection of 5 February 1954 and the March 1954 American Vogue

segments.name: The Ritz, the Grave, and the File

stops.name: Paris, Hotel Ritz: the last evening
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; one quotation of the last words is dated 9 January and the death 10 January, and the day of the words is not adjudicated here. The pin is the atlas canonical Ritz coordinate
stops.campa: She dies in her suite at the Ritz, eighty-seven years old, having worked on the coming collection days before. She had lived in the hotel for more than thirty years, walked to the rue Cambon in the morning and back at night, and kept no other home. Her maid is in the room and nobody else is. The Prefecture file, the Madrid journey, and the petition of 1941 are at this point known to a handful of French officials and to nobody at all who will sit down to write her obituary in the morning.
stops.quote: You see, this is how you die.
stops.quote_source: Chanel's last words to her maid, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The Chanel suite at the Ritz Paris, occupied from 1937 to 1971

stops.name: Paris, Eglise de la Madeleine: the funeral
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month only; the day of the funeral is not recorded in the sources consulted, and the default day used here falls earlier in the month than the death it follows
stops.campa: The funeral is held at the Madeleine. Salvador Dali comes, and Marlene Dietrich, and Yves Saint Laurent. Her own models sit in the front pews in her suits, so that from the back of the church the service reads as a showing. The obituaries call her the woman who took women out of the corset, which is true and is the whole of what they say. None of them mentions Madrid, because in January 1971 the file that would put Madrid in an obituary is still in a French archive and unread.
suggested_refs: The Eglise de la Madeleine and the January 1971 funeral

stops.name: Lausanne, Bois-de-Vaux Cemetery
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month only; the day is not recorded. The coordinate is corrected by some 900 metres, and the two lenses of this research pass supplied two different wrong values for this grave that also disagreed with each other
stops.campa: She is buried not in France but in Lausanne, in the Bois-de-Vaux cemetery, area nine, plot one hundred and twenty-nine, in the country she went to when Paris was still deciding what to do with people like her. Five stone lions are carved on the stone, read as her sign, Leo, and said to have been specified by her. The reading is interpretation laid over an attested carving. The grave is tended and visited, and it is four hundred and fifty miles from the rue Cambon.
suggested_refs: The Chanel grave at Bois-de-Vaux, area 9, plot 129, with its five lions

stops.name: Paris, the Prefecture file: agent F 7124
stops.date_confidence: attested year of publication; no month recorded. The provenance of the F 7124 reference has been corrected: it comes from a Prefecture de Police document published by Vaughan in 2011, three years before the French declassification of late 2014 that one lens credited with it
stops.campa: Hal Vaughan, looking in the French archives for something else, finds a Prefecture de Police document listing a couturier and perfumer, pseudonym Westminster, agent reference F 7124, signalled as suspect. Sleeping with the Enemy: Coco Chanel's Secret War comes out forty years after her death and the press re-reads the whole life. The house answers that she had a relationship with a German aristocrat during the war and that it clearly was not the best period for that. A further French declassification follows in 2014.
stops.quote: I was looking for something else and I come across this document saying 'Chanel is a Nazi agent' ... I really started hunting through all of the archives ... and I came across not one, but 20, 30, 40 absolutely solid archival materials
stops.quote_source: Hal Vaughan, interview with the Associated Press on the publication of Sleeping with the Enemy, quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Coco Chanel'
suggested_refs: The Prefecture de Police document naming agent F 7124, pseudonym Westminster

stops.name: Paris, Palais Galliera: Fashion Manifesto
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of opening; the run closed in August 2021 and the tour reached the Victoria and Albert Museum in September 2023
stops.campa: The Palais Galliera mounts Gabrielle Chanel: Fashion Manifesto, which travels on to Tokyo, Melbourne, and the Victoria and Albert Museum. The Metropolitan Museum's Costume Institute had done its own Chanel show in 2005 and folds her back into its Lagerfeld retrospective in 2023. The garments are hung and lit and written about at length. The occupation gets a wall panel where it gets anything at all, and a visitor who wants Madrid has to bring Madrid in with them.
suggested_refs: Gabrielle Chanel: Fashion Manifesto, Palais Galliera 2020-2021, V&A 2023
sources: Palais Galliera and V&A exhibition records

stops.name: France, the card from the ERIC network
stops.date_confidence: attested year of surfacing; no month recorded, and the place of the find is not stated in any source consulted, so the canonical Paris coordinate stands in. The card's own issuance date is 1957
stops.campa: A card surfaces stating that Chanel belonged to the ERIC network of the Resistance. Justine Picardie presents it; the historian Guillaume Pollack disputes it, noting that the card was issued in 1957, twelve years after the war, and shows evidence of alteration with white-out. No wartime record corroborates it. The two positions stand where they were left. It is the last document in the file and it does the same work as the first ones: a story about her origin, told afterward, by someone with a reason.
suggested_refs: The disputed ERIC network membership card, issued 1957, surfaced 2023
